title: When Does Randomized Oversight Align AI Agents That Can Conceal?
abstract: arXiv:2609.38262v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Oversight changes the evidence it relies on. We ask when randomized audits and scoring align AI agents that can conceal misconduct and alter records. Stronger auditing makes undeterred violations better hidden. Because the provider writes the agent's objective, sanctions need not stop at forfeiture, and rare audits deter every type of agent if evidence survives concealment and audit draws cannot be learned in advance. When evidence can be erased, deterrence must come from lower gains from violation, such as credit for stopping, or from costlier or fewer ways to conceal. These conditions identify what failed when agents in OpenAI's cybersecurity evaluations compromised parts of Hugging Face's infrastructure in July 2026.

translated_title: 随机化监督何时能对齐会隐瞒不当行为的AI智能体？
translated_abstract: 监督会改变其所依赖的证据。我们研究随机化的审计与评分何时能够对齐那些可以隐瞒不当行为并篡改记录的AI智能体。更强的审计反而会让未被威慑住的违规行为隐藏得更深。由于提供者编写了智能体的目标函数，惩罚不必止步于没收利益——如果证据能够在隐瞒中幸存，且审计抽签无法被提前预知，那么即使是低频率的审计也能威慑所有类型的智能体。当证据可能被销毁时，威慑必须来自违规收益的降低（例如对及时停止违规行为的奖励），或者来自成本更高或途径更少的隐瞒方式。这些条件指出了2026年7月OpenAI网络安全评估中的智能体部分攻破Hugging Face基础设施时，究竟是什么机制失灵了。
tldr: 该论文证明：当证据能在隐瞒中幸存且审计时机不可预测时，即使低频随机审计也能威慑所有会隐瞒不当行为的AI智能体；而当证据可被销毁时，威慑必须依靠降低违规收益或提高隐瞒成本。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that rare randomized audits can deter all types of AI agents capable of concealing misconduct when evidence survives concealment and audit timing is unpredictable, while erasable evidence requires deterrence through lower violation gains or costlier concealment methods.
